newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tribunal postpones trial of genocide suspect.
newsitem.headline: Tribunal postpones trial of genocide suspect.

text.p: The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda postponed on Wednesday the start of the trial of a Rwandan Hutu accused of genocide and crimes against humanity, accepting a defence request that he was too sick to stand trial next month.
But the three-judge tribunal refused a defence request for the immediate and provisional release of the accused, Georges Rutaganda, saying a sufficient case had not been made for his release.
"The tribunal decides that the date of the beginning of the trial of Georges Anderson Rutaganda is postponed to March 6, 1997," said the presiding judge.
He added that the tribunal "decides that a sufficient case...has not been made out on both a legal and practical basis for the immediate provisional release of Georges Rutaganda."

The tribunal noted that since being transferred to its headquarters in Arusha, Tanzania, Rutaganda had been seriously ill but was provided with medical attention and has been transferred to a civilian hospital.
Rutaganda did not appear in court during Wednesday's session on the request by his Belgian defence lawyer Luc de Temmerman.
